chunks: 3906 - And in the narration of Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about sharecropping with the people of kharaj land on the basis of a quarter, a third, or a half. He said: “There is no harm. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله accepted Khaybar on terms with its people; he gave it to the Jews when it was conquered on the basis of al-khabr, and al-khabr is half.”

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: on the basis of one-third of the yield
key_terms.النِّصْفِ: on the basis of one-half of the yield
key_terms.الْخَبْرِ: the contractual basis mentioned here, explained in the hadith as half
key_terms.الْخَرَاجِ: taxed land subject to kharaj levy
key_terms.بِالرُّبُعِ: on the basis of one-quarter of the yield
key_terms.خَيْبَرَ: Khaybar, cited as the historical precedent

ai.seo_question: Is sharecropping with kharaj landholders on a fractional yield basis permissible in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting sharecropping arrangements with the people of kharaj lands on agreed fractional shares such as one-quarter, one-third, or one-half. The Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling by citing the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with the people of Khaybar, making it a precedent in agricultural contracts.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3906 - In a narration from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said:

I asked Imam (as) about farming partnerships with the people of kharaj lands based on a quarter, a third, or half of the yield.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) made an agreement with the Jews of Khaybar when it was conquered, granting them the land based on 'al-khabr,' and 'al-khabr' means half."
